nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.rationale: Recommended because every role uses it by default.

nodes.label: No API Keys Gate
nodes.rationale: No server-wide provider keys, so users without a saved key cannot run anything; frontend locks UI but backend is the real gate, so a failed key check locks nothing.

nodes.label: Evidence clerk model
nodes.rationale: Must have built-in web search so source links are provider citations, never model-written URLs; personas only cite pages actually retrieved.

nodes.label: Document fetch with SSRF protection
nodes.rationale: Only public http(s) addresses accepted; private IPs, odd ports, credentials refused; redirects re-checked; size and time capped.

nodes.label: Multiple API keys and rotation
nodes.rationale: Round robin across keys spreads load over separate rate limits; failed keys are parked so others continue.

nodes.label: Step 3: Anonymous peer review
nodes.rationale: Anonymized, shuffled responses keep review unbiased; rankings mapped back server-side and averaged.

nodes.label: Vercel Services deployment
nodes.rationale: Async steps return 202 and run via waitUntil so each step has its own time budget.

nodes.label: PersonaAvatar
nodes.rationale: Per-member hue only aids recognition, never carries meaning.

nodes.label: Council Graph
nodes.rationale: Single per-session graph showing how the council reached its verdict, built only from stored data with no extra model calls; an aid to reading, not a replacement for the results page.

nodes.label: CSS Design Tokens (:root)
nodes.rationale: Tokens in frontend/src/style.css; dark default, light via prefers-color-scheme.

nodes.label: Seeded Force-Directed Layout (d3-force)
nodes.rationale: Tuned for stability: positions seeded from node id so a session always looks the same, persisted across reloads so the picture doesn't jump, pre-settled off-screen. Plain SVG suffices since a session has at most six members.

nodes.label: Graph Data Contract { nodes, edges }
nodes.rationale: Built by a pure backend function from stored rows; frontend filters layers but never computes structure.

nodes.label: Graph Node Kinds (persona, verdict, chairman, final_verdict, review, evidence, source)
nodes.norm_label: graph node kinds (persona, verdict, chairman, final_verdict, review, evidence, source)
nodes.rationale: Every node is a small flat circle; kind carried by colour group rather than shape, following Obsidian.

nodes.label: Peer Ranking Edges
nodes.rationale: Stored one row per (reviewer, reviewed) pair; drawn as lines by default (thicker = higher rank) or as review nodes with ?detail=reviews. Pull weakly at 2.2x link distance so the member ring doesn't collapse.

nodes.label: Obsidian-Style Visual System
nodes.rationale: Calm, dense note-taking feel: dark quiet background, thin borders, small text, single purple accent, colour only where it carries meaning.

nodes.label: Cross-Session Graph (dropped)
nodes.rationale: Dropped because users have few sessions (about 5, at most 20), so the graph would be mostly isolated dots.

nodes.label: Graph List View (Text Equivalent)
nodes.rationale: Anything shown in the graph must also be reachable as text; default under 480px.

nodes.label: Graph Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: No editing (graph is derived, not authored), no cross-session graph, no 3D/minimap/plugins.

nodes.label: Score vs. Peer-Rank Mismatch
nodes.rationale: The main thing the graph exists to show: where a member's own score diverges from how peers ranked them, which is where the interesting story is.

nodes.label: Stepper-as-Tabs
nodes.rationale: Evidence, Verdicts, Peer Review, Decision, Graph steps with state; opens on the step needing attention; kept in ?tab=.

nodes.label: View State in URL
nodes.rationale: Graph ?view=list, ?detail=reviews, ?node=<id>; session ?tab=; settings ?section= so state is shareable and restorable.
